description: Municipality-level official land prices for Japanese ski markets, 2026 公示地価 (Published Land Prices) with 基準地価 (Prefectural Land Survey) where available. Values are averages across all survey points in the municipality and mix residential, commercial and industrial land — they indicate direction, not the price of any specific parcel.

source.primary_publication_note: The MLIT portal page is dated 令和8年3月18日. The press release fetched separately reported 2026-03-17. Both dates are recorded; the one-day discrepancy is likely announcement versus publication and is not material, but it is not silently reconciled.
source.retrieved_via_note: Figures retrieved from tochidai.info, an aggregator that republishes official MLIT land-price data by municipality. Tier 4. Independently corroborates the per-market figures previously recorded as UNVERIFIED from commercial commentary, to within rounding.
source.verification_note: Two independent secondary sources now agree on Hakuba, Kutchan and Myoko to within 0.01-0.02 percentage points. Direct retrieval from MLIT remains outstanding and is required before these figures support a final recommendation.

fx_note: No AUD conversion applied. Converting requires a sourced rate and rate date (core/models/common.py refuses conversion without one). AUD figures will be added when an FX source is registered.

municipalities.notes: National rank 1 for residential appreciation. Benchmark point 白馬-1 at ¥27,400/m² rose 33.0%, after 29.6% the previous year. Commercial point 白馬5-1 at ¥40,300/m² rose 35.2%, national rank 3.
National rank 2. Notably absent from the 'emerging market' promotional narrative despite outperforming every market except Hakuba.
By far the highest absolute level of any ski municipality here - roughly 4.7x Hakuba and 6.1x Myoko. Hirafu benchmark reported at ¥189,000/m², +21.9% (UNVERIFIED).
Down roughly 85% from its 1993 peak and still falling 33 years later, despite direct Shinkansen access from Tokyo. The clearest available evidence that cheap and accessible does not mean undervalued.

The central finding. Myoko bottomed in 2022 and has recovered only ~5%, still declining year-on-year in 2026, while being promoted as the emerging market of choice. The anticipated repricing has not yet appeared in official land values.

not_in_top_ranking.note: Absent from the retrieved ranking extract. This means 'not established', not 'no change'. Retrieve individually before drawing any conclusion.
